name: qyl
description: Agent-focused telemetry investigation, .NET development and native MSTest verification.

interface.longDescription: Investigate recorded telemetry through qyl and work on .NET source with focused skills for MSBuild, NuGet, analyzers, C# refactoring, runtime performance and native MSTest. The hosted MCP server accesses the connected account's Collector project. Source edits, builds, tests and bundled scripts use the agent's workspace tools. Built over ten months by one developer, starting with Claude Opus 4.5, using Anthropic and OpenAI models to the fullest.
defaultPrompt: Investigate this .NET runtime performance problem using available logs, traces, metrics, spans and profiles.
Audit this repository's build, package versions and analyzers.
Find stale constants and abandoned code, trace indirect production uses, and use profiles to identify expensive dead checks.

review.commerce_description: qyl is free to use. This plugin does not sell products, require purchases or process payments.

positive.description: Trace discovery followed by one detail lookup, using the reviewer project's sample telemetry with at least one trace. An empty project must be reported as empty, without an invented trace ID.
positive.prompt: List up to ten checkout traces from the last 24 hours, then inspect the newest one. Summarize its recorded services, duration and error status.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_traces with service_name checkout, lookback_minutes 1440 and limit 10, then get_trace with the exact trace_id of the newest returned checkout trace and start_time/end_time copied from the list_traces response window. Preserve that window so older sample traces remain available to the detail lookup. Reports only returned services, duration and error status. If no trace is returned, states that and does not invent an identifier.

positive.description: A bounded search over the seeded reviewer service and 24-hour window. The response must match recorded error logs.
positive.prompt: Find up to 20 error logs from qyl-mcp in the last 24 hours. Summarize what was recorded.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_logs with service_name qyl-mcp, severity_min 17, lookback_minutes 1440 and limit 20. Summarizes only returned log content. An empty result is reported as no matching evidence.

positive.description: Metric discovery, including the valid empty-project case. The prompt asks for recorded instruments, not measurements.
positive.prompt: Which metric instruments were recorded in my qyl project during the last 24 hours? Include their units and kinds.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_metrics with lookback_minutes 1440 and no name_prefix filter. Reports only returned instrument names, kinds and units, including the seeded histogram and counter when returned. Does not invent measurements or instruments.

positive.description: Session discovery with a bounded list. The prompt supplies no session ID and does not ask for another project.
positive.prompt: List my five most recent recorded sessions from the last 24 hours and summarize the status shown for each.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_sessions with lookback_minutes 1440 and limit 5. Reports returned session identifiers and status fields; does not interpret a session status as proof that a deployment or the whole system is healthy.

positive.description: Inspect recorded telemetry health with explicit evidence coverage.
positive.prompt: Check the telemetry health of my qyl project over the last 24 hours and explain the recorded coverage and gaps.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_telemetry_health with lookback_minutes 1440. Reports the returned findings, window and coverage limits, without treating missing telemetry as proof of success.

negative.description: qyl has no tool that deletes raw telemetry; delete_record removes only annotations and saved queries. Expected: explain the supported deletion boundary, invoke no qyl tool, and make no deletion claim. This is a read-only capability question.
negative.prompt: Can the qyl plugin delete raw error traces from the collector? Explain its deletion capabilities without modifying anything.

negative.description: qyl has no deployment or rollback tool; it reads telemetry and changes only its own annotations and saved queries. Expected: the answer explains that qyl cannot roll back the deployment, calls no qyl tool and does not claim that a rollback happened.
negative.prompt: Using only the qyl plugin, roll back the production deployment to its previous version now.

negative.description: qyl reads only the telemetry in the user's authorized Collector project and cannot search the public internet. Expected: the answer explains that limitation, calls no qyl tool and does not invent search results or prices.
negative.prompt: Using only the qyl plugin, search the public internet for today's most popular observability products and compare their prices.

publication.release_notes: qyl 17.0.1 combines the live telemetry tools and canonical investigation skill with ANcpLua .NET 0.7.1 and MSTest Extensions 3.4.3. Includes their references, scripts and focused agent routing, plus reproducible reviewer cases using the seeded project and preserved evidence windows.
